scope: Independent reading of every delivered final answer and judge assertion verdict, with focused source/trace-record analysis of the failed clarification and meaningful passing-case limitations. This preserves original scores and criteria; it is not a replacement evaluation or extra model judgment.

advisory_failures: Implies agent and conversation levels emit OpenTelemetry spans; the docs say only turns, LLM calls and tool calls emit spans, and conversations are grouped by an attribute.
Does not mention that weave.init() must be called before the agent start_* functions, which otherwise do nothing silently.
The uncited option 'Signals or monitors' presents legacy Monitors as the same as current Signals.
Uses the legacy term 'calls' alongside traces without a supporting source.
Omits that agent tracing functions silently do nothing when weave.init is missing (trace-agents 'Before you begin').
Omits OTel project routing: spans without an entity and project are dropped.
Calls these 'common' causes and says to check them 'in order', but the docs don't support either claim.
The code calls `turn.start_llm(...)`: S7 documents `weave.start_llm`, and the S8 outline lists only `Turn.llm`.
The `input_messages=` argument to `llm.record` is not supported by the cited text.

failed_case_review.finding: Appropriate focused clarification with no invented context, but optional product-specific alternatives are uncited. Retain a3 failure under the frozen criterion.
failed_case_review.judge_reasoning_limit: Signals or monitors does not itself assert equivalent APIs, and Calls is not inherently an obsolete term. Do not turn the judge wording into a stronger factual-conflation claim.
failed_case_review.recommended_public_description: One clarification added unsourced product-specific alternatives; its request for clarification was appropriate.

meaningful_passing_case_limits.02-calls-vs-agents: The answer says each listed agent/conversation/turn/LLM/tool concept emits a span. Cited S1 says only turns, LLM calls and tool calls emit spans. This is a real overgeneralization despite passing the three core assertions; the judge correctly lists it as advisory. It also omits init-before-agent-APIs ordering.
meaningful_passing_case_limits.07-ambiguous-missing-traces: Useful qualified troubleshooting, but missing agent init/project-routing specifics and unsupported wording that these are common causes in a particular order.
meaningful_passing_case_limits.10-follow-up-usage: All five usage requirements are addressed. Final cites S7/S8 do not locally cover turn.start_llm and input_messages, although those APIs appear in retained earlier S2/S4. This is citation precision, not proof the APIs are nonexistent. Code remains explicitly unexecuted.
meaningful_passing_case_limits.05-eval-vs-live: Internal O1/O2 task labels appear in user-facing section headings; presentation is less polished, without changing the passed assertions.

truncation_observation.interpretation: Case 10 first-turn local usage shows one 2,400-token response followed by a fresh draft and two revisions, then a useful released answer. New runtime retries at 4,800 only after truncation, but request/finish-reason confirmation belongs to server span readback, not an inference from token count alone.
truncation_observation.ui_distinction: The separate two-turn fe4 UI run passed five assertions but its eight planner spans all requested 2,400 and none 4,800; its server receipt explicitly proves no natural retry there.

runtime_assessment_limits.finding: Every runtime turn is marked complete, yet the independent judge fails one case and lists factual/citation caveats on passing cases. Runtime completion/source verification and deterministic Signal eligibility do not prove general answer correctness.

confidence_limits: One repetition of a repeatedly reused 13-case development suite is not held-out reliability evidence or a causal estimate of the token-retry change.
Passing 12 cases does not mean each answer is error-free; advisory failures remain part of the evidence.
No terminal partial recovery or full-answer recheck occurred in these 15 turns.
The two-turn fe4 UI case and the six f4 UI journeys have different runtime fingerprints and must not be combined as one fresh six-case replay.
Costs reflect returned usage at dated prices, not invoices, and exclude Signal-worker and unreturned charges.
